summary: Quarterly pipeline sprint between Redwood and Cascade Alliance to align on co-sell handoffs, risk triage for top accounts, and next steps for pilot activation. Key themes: lead routing, pricing guardrails, technical benchmark (latency/cost), SSO/contract SOW path, and a joint customer outreach plan.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-14 15:00 PDT — Duration: 52m
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Zoe (Redwood CSM); Daniel, Aisha, Tomás, Leah (Cascade)

Summary: quick sprint to align co-sell pipeline. Referenced: shared spreadsheet (Cascade-RW-co-sell-2026.xlsx), playbook deck (link).

00:00 Morgan: okay everyone good to go? um, hey thanks for squeezing this in, we wanted to keep it tight, 45-ish minutes but apparently we have 52, so nice.
00:18 Daniel: yeah thanks Morgan, appreciate it. quick context — Leah wanted a straight run down of the top accounts and where we have risk, and also how we route leads.
00:29 Morgan: perfect. Priya, quick intro?
00:33 Priya: hi all, SE for the account, I'll own the technical bench and the latency/cost runs. uh, expect some noise around peaks, but we'll enumerate.
00:43 Aisha: great, and Tomás from ops will handle the handoff for CRM routing and lead scoring.
00:49 Zoe: hey, I'll coordinate onboarding and ensure the pilot success metrics get tracked in the CSM board.
00:56 01:02 Morgan: cool. Slide one — account list. we classified 12 accounts into A/B/C. top 4 A accounts: Meridian Systems, Harbortek, NuroGen, and SlateCity. question for Cascade: are any of those already in your direct pipeline or owned by a reseller?
01:18 Tomás: Meridian and Harbortek — Meridian is in our channel pipeline, they're hot but they've got existing vendor commitments. Harbortek is more open. SlateCity is likely to be owned by their internal infra team so that's medium risk. NuroGen is early discovery.
01:31 Morgan: okay sounds like Harbortek is our best joint near-term opportunity then. we propose a canary pilot there.
01:37 Aisha: agreed. what are Redwood's recommended success criteria for a pilot?
01:41 Priya: technically we want to validate 95th pctl latency under 800ms for the typical prompt set and cost per 1k tokens at or below the threshold we outlined in the spreadsheet. quality regressions also must be flagged in the eval harness.
01:56 Daniel: can you restate that — 95th percentile 800ms? that's pretty tight.
01:59 Priya: yeah, for the hosted path, for dedicated we can tighten. but, uh, the 800ms is for user-facing experiences.
02:08 Morgan: also worth noting we support auto-fallback to small-quantized variants if peak capacity or cost is too high, that helps keep the UX alive.
02:18 Leah: hold on, when you say "quantized variants" will that change output quality? 
02:22 Priya: short answer — minimally for many workloads, though some creative generation may show differences; we'll surface that in the benchmark report.
02:31 Daniel: ok got it. next — lead routing. Tomás you mentioned CRM ownership — walk us through current flow.
02:38 Tomás: sure. by default leads hit Cascade's SDR queue; we have a rule to forward anything tagged "enterprise-llm" to partners@cascade, which is monitored by Aisha. then partners triage and either assign to Cascade AE or hand off to partner (Redwood) for direct outreach. the issue is timing — there's up to a 48h delay.
02:57 Morgan: 48 hours is long for these - we recommend a 6-hour SLA for handoffs on joint accounts; we can set up a webhook to push lead details to Redwood's partner portal immediately.
03:10 Aisha: that'd be ideal. are there security concerns sending lead data? we need to check PII flow.
03:16 Zoe: we'll only send minimal lead metadata — name, company, role, and inferred intent score. no transcripts or content unless consented.
03:25 Tomás: ok, need to confirm CRM field mapping. action: Morgan to share field map and Priya to validate for the webhook.
03:34 Morgan: noted. next — pricing guardrails. we've proposed a co-sell discount tier for pilot accounts in the sheet. Tomás, would Cascade be comfortable with a shared-convert commission model or prefer flat discount?
03:46 Tomás: we prefer the shared-convert because it aligns incentives, but margin discussions with finance will be needed.
03:52 Morgan: okay we'll put both options in the playbook.
03:55 04:00 Aisha: question on procurement and SOW — what is Redwood's standard SOW timeline? we have legal review cycles that are 3 weeks on average.
04:07 Zoe: for pilots we use a simplified SOW template to accelerate — usually two weeks if legal is responsive.
04:12 Leah: we need SOC2/ISO cert copies before any data sharing.
04:16 Priya: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 current, we can share the cert bundle and the compliance pack. note — if account requires on-prem or VPC, that will add time.
04:27 Daniel: good to know. NuroGen is in healthcare vertical; likely extra compliance checks.
04:33 Morgan: then for NuroGen we should plan for the Private deployment path early. maybe kick a parallel track for regulatory scoping.
04:41 Aisha: yes let's do that. Priya — can you include a Private deployment checklist in the benchmark?
04:45 Priya: yep.
04:47 05:00 Morgan: moving on to risk triage — what are the top three risks per account?
05:03 Tomás: 1) incumbent entrenchment at Meridian, 2) data residency needs at NuroGen, 3) timing constraints at SlateCity (quarterly budget freeze).
05:12 Morgan: for Meridian the fallback is a joint exec intro and demo; for NuroGen prep the Private path; for SlateCity consider a proof-of-concept scoped to a single business unit.
05:21 Aisha: okay that sounds practical.
05:24 06:00 Daniel: technical question — how does Redwood's KV cache and prefix caching work across shared vs dedicated? sometimes our infra person hears KV "cash" and gets confused.
06:10 Priya: (laughs) yeah KV cash is not a thing. the KV cache stores token keys for recent sequences to reduce recomputation across requests. in dedicated pools cache is local to the GPU pool unless you enable a shared-layer cache which we can discuss.
06:24 Daniel: that makes sense. if we run benchmarks, can you show both shared and dedicated configs?
06:29 Priya: will do. we'll include three configs: hosted default, dedicated reserved, and private on-prem simulation.
06:36 07:00 Morgan: about instrumentation — we need to pull token-level cost traces into your CRM for transparency. Zoe, do you own that report?
07:07 Zoe: yes i'll own it, we'll map tokens by request route and show cost delta per model variant.
07:12 Tomás: perfect, that's helpful for finance.
07:15 08:00 Aisha: a quick objection we often hear from prospects — switching inference providers risks vendor lock and retraining costs. how do we address that?
08:09 Morgan: main pitch — we keep model-agnostic routes and compatibility layers; customers can pin model versions and even bring their own model via private deployment. plus the rollback and A/B features help mitigate risk.
08:23 Aisha: makes sense. Daniel: competitor callouts? we've heard EdgeServe offers deeper reseller margins.
08:30 Morgan: EdgeServe's offering is margin-heavy but lacks the cost telemetry and rollout tools we provide; ModelFlow touts orchestration but doesn't have our latency SLOs. we'll document these differentiators in the one-pager.
08:44 09:00 Tomás: logistics — what's the expected internal Redwood cadence for lead response? Morgan you said 6 hours. Is that real?
09:07 Morgan: yes for pilot A accounts we can commit to 6 hours business hours, otherwise 24 hours for B/C.
09:13 Tomás: ok good.
09:15 10:00 Morgan: let's talk pilot timeline. propose: week 0-1 align playbook and legal contact, week 2-3 technical benchmark, week 4 joint outreach and demo, week 5 feedback and contract. any blockers?
10:13 Leah: finance needs the pricing band to sign off; can we provide a 30/60/90 pricing schedule?
10:19 Morgan: yes we'll provide that in the spreadsheet — the co-sell tab has suggested bands.
10:23 Priya: question — do you prefer a full-service Redwood-led demo or a joint demo with Cascade sales?
10:29 Aisha: joint demo is better for credibility with the customer.
10:32 Morgan: noted. we'll prepare a joint demo script and pass roles to you.
10:36 11:00 Daniel: one more technical gotcha — for Harbortek they use an internal embeddings stack, will Redwood support hybrid embeddings storage?
11:09 Priya: we can, but it's an advanced config — we have to align on vector store compatibility and encryption at rest. may require the Private path.
11:18 Daniel: okay mark as medium risk.
11:21 12:00 Morgan: quick check — shared artifacts. link to playbook and sheet in chat. also the demo script template.
12:08 Zoe: i'll upload updated CSM checklist to the shared folder, and create a Slack channel for daily updates during pilot.
12:15 Tomás: will invite the CRM team.
12:20 13:00 Morgan: open mic for any other issues?
13:05 Leah: can Redwood provide a short one-page SOC2 summary for execs?
13:10 Zoe: yes, we'll attach the compliance pack.
13:14 Aisha: about incentives — Cascade wants joint case study language in pilot agreement. any objections?
13:20 Morgan: no, but legal will want approval rights on quote and release timing.
13:24 Aisha: understood.
13:27 14:00 Daniel: if we hit pilot success, what's the scale plan? dedicated pools or hybrid?
14:06 Priya: scale decision depends on peak qps and cost sensitivity — typical path: start hosted, then move to dedicated reserve if sustained throughput>X or latency needs tighten. we'll show thresholds in the benchmark.
14:18 Morgan: and our Optimize toolkit will recommend quantization profiles to reduce cost.
14:22 15:00 Aisha: can you include an estimate of unit economics per seat or per active user?
15:06 Morgan: yes, we'll produce a model in the spreadsheet.
15:11 16:00 (brief cross talk)
16:05 Tomás: we also have an upcoming partner summit — could Redwood present a short session?
16:09 Morgan: yep happy to. Priya can co-present the technical piece.
16:14 Priya: sure.
16:16 17:00 Morgan: ok time check — ten minutes left, let's recap next steps.
17:08 Morgan: 1) Morgan to send field map + playbook + pricing by 2026-10-18 — action.
17:15 Priya: 2) run benchmarks for 3 pilot configs and share report by 2026-10-26.
17:20 Zoe: 3) upload CSM checklist and create Slack channel by EOD 2026-10-14.
17:24 Leah: 4) I'll confirm legal contact and timeline by 2026-10-16.
17:29 Tomás: 5) Cascade to nominate pilot accounts by 2026-10-20.
17:33 Morgan: perfect. any final Qs?
17:35 Daniel: no, that's good. thanks everyone.
17:39 Morgan: thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts. meeting adjourned.

Action items (as spoken in call):
- Priya Nair - run latency + cost benchmark for top 3 pilot accounts - 2026-10-26
- Morgan Ellis - update co-sell lead routing doc and share with Tomás - 2026-10-18
- Leah Beck - confirm legal contact for SOW and send intro - 2026-10-16

References mentioned: Cascade-RW-co-sell-2026.xlsx, co-sell-playbook-v3.pdf, demo-script-template.pptx

End of transcript.
